drug_class: Opioid combination pain reliever / Narcotic analgesic
purpose: This medication is used to relieve moderate to moderately severe pain, such as pain after surgery, dental procedures, or injuries. It combines two pain relievers that work together to give you better relief than either one alone. It may also sometimes be used to help with a cough.
how_it_works: Acetaminophen (the same ingredient in regular Tylenol) works in your brain to reduce pain signals and lower fever. Codeine is a mild opioid, which means it attaches to special receptors in your brain and nervous system to block pain messages and make you feel more comfortable. Together, they tackle pain from two different angles at the same time.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, nausea or upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, and lightheadedness are the most common side effects. You may also feel a little foggy or have a harder time concentrating. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can seriously damage your liver and increase drowsiness. Do not take more than directed, since too much acetaminophen can cause liver damage. Codeine can be habit-forming, so only take it as prescribed and never share it with others. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, kidney problems, breathing problems, or a history of substance use disorder. Call 911 immediately if you notice slow or shallow breathing, extreme drowsiness, or confusion.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain, but never more than prescribed. Do not take more than your doctor tells you to, and do not take it more often than directed. Always follow the specific instructions on your prescription label since doses can vary depending on the strength prescribed.
